title: Sum of the Even Numbers
oneLiner: Loop over a list, keep only the even numbers, and add them up, negative numbers included.
keyTakeaway: Test evenness with n % 2 == 0, never with n % 2 == 1 for odd: in C# a negative odd number gives -1, not 1. Loop, filter with an if, accumulate into a variable that starts at 0.
explanation:
Return the sum of the even numbers in the list. An empty list, or one with no even numbers, sums to 0. The list can contain negative numbers, and negative even numbers count.

This is the loop-filter-accumulate shape you'll use constantly: start a total at 0, loop over every number, and add it only if it passes a test. A number is even when dividing by 2 leaves no remainder: n % 2 == 0.

Watch the negative case. In C#, -3 % 2 is -1 (the remainder takes the sign of the left side), so an "is it odd?" test written as n % 2 == 1 misses negative odd numbers. In Python -3 % 2 is 1, so the same test happens to work there. Testing n % 2 == 0 is correct in both. When it passes, try the one-line versions: nums.Where(n => n % 2 == 0).Sum() in C#, sum(n for n in nums if n % 2 == 0) in Python.

visualizationSteps.message: Done: 6. Note -3 % 2 is -1 in C#, which is why "== 1" is the wrong odd test.

complexity.note: One pass over the n numbers with a single running total.
